test_title: PYST 15: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 26 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question: What does the phrase ‘religious orthodoxy’ mean?

options.text: The traditional beliefs of a religious group
The advanced beliefs of a political group
The western beliefs of a business group
The modern beliefs of a social group

solution:
The correct answer is: **The traditional beliefs of a religious group**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation:** The phrase** 'religious orthodoxy' **refers to the adherence to the traditional and established beliefs and practices of a religious group.
 
• In the context of the passage, it** highlights** how certain religious officials use these traditional beliefs to dominate and influence people, thereby promoting superstitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The advanced beliefs of a political group:** This is not relevant to the context, as the passage speaks about traditional religious beliefs, not political beliefs.
 
• **The western beliefs of a business group:** This option does not fit the context. The passage is discussing religious beliefs, not the beliefs of a business group.
 
• **The modern beliefs of a social group:** This is incorrect because 'orthodoxy' typically refers to traditional rather than modern beliefs.
